messages:
alex: quick heads-up. ran into a weird inconsistency in the migration spike: a delete from client A showed up on node-old, then a concurrent write landed and node-new applied it later — tombstone ended up "after" the write in the final log.

maria: can you paste the minimal trace? was the gateway routing already switched when the second write hit?

alex: snippet from traces: 
```
migration.start id=mig-77 -> new=node-11
node-old: mark=draining lease=77 ts=161771 apply del:k=prefix:x:42
client write seq=900 -> routed to gateway-3 -> gateway routed to node-old (race) -> node-old accepted locally
node-new: started accepting after metadata flip, then applied same write seq=900
compaction: tombstone epoch tag=77 vs write epoch tag=76 -> ordering wrong
```
we didn't lose ops but ordering rules and epoch tags created ambiguous result.

tyler: sounds like we have three orthogonal knobs to consider: prevent writers from hitting old owner during migration, make forwards durable/serial, or make apply idempotent and resolve order deterministically.

jen: gate-level routing change is simplest for hot keys: gateway learns a drain hint and switches routing to new owner for writes immediately. downside: slow hint propagation for large fleets.

sam: agree. On the other hand we can implement a tiny migration journal on the old owner: any write received during drain is synchronously replicated to new owner and recorded locally as "forwarded:op_id". That guarantees visibility if old crashes—journal can be replayed by coordinator.

li: for correctness we should encode a deterministic conflict resolution rule. propose op precedence: higher (migration_epoch, logical_seq) wins. tombstone wins only if its migration_epoch >= write.migration_epoch. Tie resolved by uuid. That keeps resolution local and deterministic.

maria: ok but how do we make sure gateways and clients don't observe higher tail latency because of sync forwards? For cold keys it's fine, hot keys we should prefer gateway hinting first.

tyler: hybrid: try fast-path hint via pubsub with best-effort; fallback for any write still routed to old -> old synchronously replicate to new (with retries) and persist to its migration-journal. after final commit, coordinator marks migration.complete and garbage collects journal.

alex: proposal for spike implementation: 
- old owner adds migration_state{epoch, draining_until, journal_id}.
- when draining, old owner forwards writes to new owner via RPC replicate_and_ack(op). replicate_and_ack persists into new_owner WAL before ack. old_owner appends op_id to local migration journal (durable).
- compaction/merge uses (migration_epoch, op_id) for deterministic ordering and idempotency. tombstone tags get migration_epoch.
- coordinator exposes pubsub hint: drain_hint(migration_epoch, new_owner) for gateway subscribers. gateway uses first-forward-as-hint to accelerate routing.

jen: plan sounds good. we should measure forward latency and journal write amplification. add metrics: migration_forward_count, migration_forward_failures, migration_journal_size.

sam: also include a crash-recovery flow in spike: if old dies mid-drain, coordinator will read journal (or ask old's lease holders) and replay outstanding ops into new before finalizing. implement a small replay API.

maria: action items: alex write RFC sketch + resolution rules; sam build spike for replicate_and_ack + journal; li add deterministic ordering rules to RFC; tyler prototype pubsub hint in gateway; jen own canary plan and metrics.

deploy-bot: spike branch created -> CI triggered.

alex: thanks all, will file tickets and attach the repro trace above. closing for now.
